subject: Pilot economics & per-model traffic allocation — confirmation needed
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@atlashealth.com>, Evan Cole <evan.cole@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot economics & per-model traffic allocation — confirmation needed

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really appreciate the clarity on the workflows. Quick recap and a concrete ask so procurement and my team can line up a pilot SOW: please confirm the per-model traffic assumptions below or flag adjustments.

Summary from the call (our interpretation):
- Primary use case: patient triage + internal knowledge assistant (chat) + semantic search across care pathways (embeddings) + a short reranker step for clinical note retrieval.
- Pilot target: 3-month technical pilot, regional US deployment, non-PHI data for the initial run.

Our recommended traffic/volume assumptions for pricing (please confirm):
1) Chat assistant (instruction-style, multi-turn):
   - Estimated 250k full-turn exchanges / month
   - Avg input prompt: 120 tokens; avg model response: 420 tokens → 540 tokens per exchange
   - Monthly tokens (chat): 250k * 540 = 135,000,000 tokens (135M)

2) Embeddings (semantic search index + similarity queries):
   - Estimated 1.2M embedding calls / month (indexing + incremental queries)
   - Avg token footprint per call: 128 tokens → 153,600,000 tokens (153.6M)

3) Reranker (light rerank on top-K):
   - Estimated 150k calls / month
   - Avg token footprint per call: 60 tokens → 9,000,000 tokens (9M)

Total estimated monthly tokens ≈ 297.6M (≈298M).

Pricing target you mentioned on the call: target unit $/1M tokens = $350. At that target the run-rate math is: 297.6 * $350 ≈ $104,160 / month.

Two quick pricing bands for procurement planning (for discussion):
- Conservative (no optimizations): $350 / 1M → ~ $104k / month
- Optimized (embedding quantization + caching + request-level batching): assume ~30% lower token bill → ~$73k / month

Questions / asks for Atlas:
- Can you confirm the raw monthly volumes above (chat 250k, embeds 1.2M, rerank 150k) or provide corrected numbers?
- Is a target committed run-rate band of $75k–$110k / month acceptable for procurement to start SOW review?
- Any constraints on embedding model fidelity vs unit-cost (i.e., would you accept a quantized embedding model if it reduces cost but retains >92% retrieval fidelity on your eval set)?

Next steps I propose after you confirm volumes:
1) We’ll provide a 3-month pilot SOW with a committed token floor and stepped overage rates.
2) Jordan will prepare a short cost-sensitivity appendix showing model-routing scenarios (e.g., higher chat share vs higher embedding share) to show impact on $/1M.
3) Ben (SE) will map a short perf checklist for the initial integration (KV cache options + batch window suggestions).

Attachments: I’ll attach a simple month-by-month token calc sheet and an initial SOW template for procurement to review.

If you can reply with the volume corrections by EOD Monday (your timezone) we’ll circulate an updated SOW by Wednesday.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments referenced: MAP_v2.xlsx (token calc), SOW_pilot_draft.pdf (initial SOW template)

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@atlashealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & per-model traffic allocation — confirmation needed

Vanessa — thanks for the concise recap and the numbers. We ran a quick traffic pull and a few corrections: we expect slightly lower embedding volume and slightly lower chat volume in month 1 of the pilot (scale-up over months 2–3). Updated numbers below (attached CSV with sample traffic snapshot):

Revised assumptions for pilot months (month 1 conservative):
- Chat exchanges: 200k / month (not 250k) — avg 540 tokens/exchange → 108M tokens
- Embeddings: 900k / month (index + queries) — avg 128 tokens → 115.2M tokens
- Reranker: 120k / month — avg 60 tokens → 7.2M tokens

Revised total: 230.4M tokens / month.

Procurement note: our internal stakeholders asked for a committed pilot band of $60k–$90k / month to greenlight the pilot. We can agree to a 3-month pilot with a committed floor if overage is clearly capped and there is a rollback path to a lower-cost embedding model if retrieval fidelity holds.

I attached the traffic_snapshot.csv (sample anonymized call volumes) and looped in procurement. Evan — can you confirm the security/compliance runbook items we discussed so we can include in SOW?

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Head of Search & Data Products | Atlas Health
sofia@atlashealth.com | +1 (617) 555-6123

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@atlashealth.com>, Evan Cole <evan.cole@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & per-model traffic allocation — confirmation needed

Thanks Sofia — good to have the conservative snapshot. Action items from my side:

1) Pricing proposal for procurement (draft will attach to HubSpot):
   - Commit: 3 months, committed floor 230M tokens / month (we'll model both month-1 conservative and month-2/3 ramp)
   - Pilot rate (proposed): $330 / 1M tokens on committed volume (net effective). That yields a committed monthly price ~= 230 * $330 = $75,900 / month.
   - Overage: $400 / 1M tokens beyond committed floor (monthly true-up).
   - Optimizations: if Atlas opts into embedding quantization + prefix caching we can drop effective cost by ~20–35% — propose a conditional credit if embedding fidelity tests pass (>92% recall on their eval prompt set).

2) SOW + security appendix: Vanessa, I’ll drop the SOW_pilot_draft.pdf into the Drive folder and include a short security/compliance checklist for the non-PHI pilot (what Evan will confirm).

3) SE checklist (Ben): please include the following in the checklist we send to engineering: KV cache TTL suggestion, recommended batch window for embeddings, suggested model routing policy (chat-first, fallback to cheaper chat-medium for short prompts), and a reranker timeout guard.

Next steps (timeline):
- Today: Jordan to upload SOW draft + cost sensitivity appendix to HubSpot/Drive (link below).
- Mon EOD: Atlas to confirm final month-1 volumes and embedding fidelity tolerance.
- Wed: Redwood to circulate SOW and pilot order form for signature.

I’ve attached the initial MAP_v2.xlsx (token calcs) and will push the SOW to the shared Drive now.

—Jordan
